business_problem: Arc XP needed its content-management platform to keep pace with hypergrowth without forcing engineers to spend increasing amounts of time managing database infrastructure instead of building new publishing and digital-experience features.
solution_summary: Arc XP built its cloud-native CMS and digital experience platform on MongoDB, then moved to MongoDB Atlas as rapid customer growth made managed operations more important than self-running database infrastructure. Atlas stores the documents at the heart of the platform—text, images, video, and metadata—and sits inside a microservices architecture running with AWS. By shifting to Atlas, Arc XP gave its engineering teams back the time they had been spending on upgrades, uptime work, and operational maintenance, while preserving the flexibility to experiment with new features for publishers and other digital brands. The platform now spans dozens of clusters and tens of thousands of collections, supports full-text content access and API-driven services, and provides the scalable foundation Arc XP needs to power thousands of sites across multiple geographies while exploring newer capabilities such as App Services and vector-enabled AI workflows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Arc XP's content documents and provides the managed data platform for its cloud-native CMS and experience services.

data_flow: Content objects such as text, images, video, and metadata are stored in MongoDB Atlas, Arc XP's microservices query and update that content for publishing and digital-experience workflows, and APIs expose the same data to publishers and downstream applications across many regions.
business_outcome: Arc XP improved developer productivity by roughly 70%, freed engineers to focus on roadmap work instead of database operations, and scaled the platform to thousands of sites and billions of monthly content interactions.
metrics: Arc XP customers typically see a 70% improvement in developer productivity.
Arc XP uses roughly 63 clusters and over 50,000 MongoDB collections.
The platform powers nearly 2,000 sites in 27 countries.
Arc XP handles 4.5 billion articles accessed by two billion unique users each month.
